concept.name: Ordinary least squares
concept.definition: The estimation method that chooses regression coefficients to minimize the sum of squared residuals between observed and fitted values, yielding the closed-form estimator beta_hat = (X'X)^{-1} X'y for the linear model. Under the Gauss-Markov assumptions it is the best linear unbiased estimator.
concept.intuition: Draw the line (or hyperplane) that makes the total of the squared vertical gaps between data and fit as small as possible; squaring punishes big misses and keeps the algebra tractable.
concept.mechanics: Minimizing ||y - X beta||^2 gives the normal equations X'X beta = X'y, solved as beta_hat = (X'X)^{-1} X'y when X has full column rank. Inference uses the residual variance s^2 = e'e/(n-k) and Var(beta_hat) = s^2 (X'X)^{-1}, with exact t- and F-tests under normal errors.
concept.formula: beta_hat = argmin_b sum_i (y_i - x_i' b)^2 = (X'X)^{-1} X'y, where X is the n x k design matrix and y the response vector.
concept.failure_modes: OLS is highly sensitive to outliers and high-leverage points, breaks down when X'X is near-singular from multicollinearity, and its standard errors are invalid under heteroskedasticity or autocorrelated errors. On unit-root data it produces spurious regressions.
concept.misconceptions: That minimizing squared error makes OLS optimal in general: its BLUE property requires exogeneity, linearity, and spherical errors, and outside those it can be dominated by GLS, ridge, or robust estimators.
concept.example: Regressing a stock's daily returns on the market's returns by OLS gives the slope minimizing squared return gaps, the standard CAPM beta estimate.

citations.source: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 4.1.4.1 Linear Least Squares Regression
